papers.title: Multi-Omics Analysis Reveals That Aβ42- Me3 Co-Aggregation Induces Mitophagy Blockade in Early Stages of Alzheimer's Disease.
papers.summary: This study looks at how amyloid-beta (Aβ42) protein clumps together with another molecule called Me3 in the early stages of Alzheimer's disease. Using multiple types of large-scale biological data (multi-omics), the researchers found that this co-aggregation blocks mitophagy, the process cells use to clear out damaged mitochondria. This blockade likely contributes to the buildup of cellular damage that characterizes early Alzheimer's pathology.
papers.why: This paper directly addresses mitophagy blockade as an early driver of neuronal dysfunction in Alzheimer's disease, providing mechanistic insight relevant to the PhD project's focus on mitophagy and autophagy failure in neurons.

papers.title: Spatial-EV-seq: Mapping the spatial organisation of extracellular vesicles in tissues.
papers.summary: Spatial-EV-seq is a new method that maps where extracellular vesicles (EVs) are located within intact tissue sections, rather than studying them in isolation after extraction. It likely combines spatial barcoding or imaging with sequencing to capture the molecular cargo of EVs while preserving their tissue location. This allows researchers to see how EV distribution and content vary across different regions of an organ or tissue.
papers.why: This technique could reveal how extracellular vesicles contribute to local signalling around neurons, interneurons, and perineuronal nets, offering a new spatial layer complementary to transcriptomics and metabolomics data in studying mitophagy-related intercellular communication.

papers.title: Xiaobanxia decoction, a compound Chinese herbal medicine, attenuates chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting via restoring AMPK/TFEB-mediated BNIP3/NIX mitophagy.
papers.summary: This study looks at Xiaobanxia decoction, a traditional Chinese herbal medicine, and tests whether it can reduce nausea and vomiting caused by chemotherapy. The researchers found that it works by restoring a cellular process called mitophagy, which clears out damaged mitochondria, through a specific molecular pathway (AMPK/TFEB) and specific mitophagy receptors (BNIP3/NIX). Essentially, the herbal remedy helps cells better manage mitochondrial quality control, which appears to relieve chemotherapy-related sickness symptoms.
papers.why: While this paper focuses on peripheral/gut-related chemotherapy side effects rather than neurons or brain tissue, it is tangentially relevant because it details AMPK/TFEB-mediated BNIP3/NIX mitophagy mechanisms that are core to the PhD project's focus on mitophagy pathways, even though the disease context and tissue differ substantially.

papers.title: Autophagy in MASLD: A Metabolic and Precision Medicine Perspective.
papers.summary: This paper discusses autophagy's role in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), formerly known as NAFLD. It frames autophagy dysregulation as a key contributor to liver metabolic disturbances and disease progression. The paper also explores how precision medicine approaches could target autophagy pathways for personalized treatment strategies.
papers.why: While this paper centers on liver disease rather than brain tissue, it may offer transferable insights into autophagy regulation mechanisms that could inform understanding of neuronal autophagy and mitophagy pathways relevant to the PhD project.
